title: Peak Capacity Cascade Playbook — dry-run notes
content:
Goal: create a simple, rehearsable cascade plan for SRE + Serving Runtime + Support so we can run a live dry-run before the Q2 product-heavy event. This is a personal scratchpad — not final wording for customers or execs, more of a rehearsal script + checklist.

High-level intent:
- Reduce customer-visible impact when GPU capacity hits a critical threshold (regional / model-family level).
- Provide clear, role-specific lines: who speaks on Slack, who updates status page, who triggers fallbacks.
- Validate communication cadence for internal stakeholders and customer-facing messages.

Key stakeholders and roles (quick):
- Incident Lead (IL): takes overall ownership of the event, declares severity, calls for runbook. (Likely SRE lead on shift)
- Runtime Ops: implements immediate routing/fallback policy changes, scales Dedicated pools if possible.
- Model Routing Owner: validates model-variant fallback compatibility and quality gates.
- Customer Success (CS): drafts and posts customer messages for impacted accounts; coordinates with Sales for named accounts.
- Product/PM: approves messaging for product-impacting decisions (e.g., soft-degrade features).
- Comms (ops-comm): crafts brief public-facing status page blurb + Slack to #prod-status.

Cascade phases (playbook outline):
1) Detection (0-2 min): automated alerts + telemetry rule trip. IL acknowledges within 2 minutes.
2) Triage (2-10 min): confirm scope (region/model/pool). Rapid check: "is this degraded or outage?"
   - If degraded: apply routing weight reduction to affected model variants.
   - If outage or risk to SLAs: initiate fallback to lower-cost variant or route to alternate region.
3) Mitigation (10-30 min): Runtime Ops runs prepared commands to: enable fallback policy, increase batch windows for non-interactive workloads, throttle non-critical jobs.
4) Customer comms (15-45 min): CS + Comms publish initial status (short and actionable).
5) Recovery & Monitoring (30-90 min): observe KPIs, rollback changes when stable.
6) After-action (24-72 hours): postmortem, customer outreach where needed.

Sample internal messages (templates)
- Slack initial: "ALERT: Region us-west-2 high GPU queue (P90 latency > 3s). IL @<name> acknowledged. Triage in progress. Please hold on non-critical deploys to us-west for next 30m. Details: JIRA-OPS-1287."
- Ops->Status page short: "Investigating elevated inference latency affecting specific model families in us-west-2. We're routing traffic to compatible variants and scaling; more updates in 30 mins."
- CS->Customer (named): "Heads up: we’re seeing elevated inference latency in us-west-2 affecting [model]. We’re routing traffic to a compatible variant to reduce impact and will follow up with ETA within 30 minutes. If you see errors, please DM our support channel."

Talking points for all-hands (30–60s bullets for execs):
- What happened (plain): "We observed an unexpected concentration of high-concurrency requests to a specific model family in one region, which pushed queueing and latency beyond SLOs."
- What we did (plain): "We ran our cascade: routing fallbacks -> temporary throttles on non-critical workloads -> burst of Dedicated capacity in the region."
- Current status: "Traffic is largely routed, latency improving; we're monitoring closely and will share a postmortem."
- Why it matters: "This is a test of our ability to keep customers served under sudden pressure and to validate our fallback policy set."

Dry-run checklist (pre-run items)
- Confirm run participants and backups (IL, Runtime, Model Routing, CS, Comms).
- Verify runbook docs reachable from Confluence and that run commands are pre-approved.
- Create a synthetic load plan (Jenkins job / loadgen) with safe limits.
- Prepare a status page entry that can be published with one click.
- Rehearse the Slack templates and who will paste them.
- Ensure dedicated contact for high-touch customers is on-call.

Run playbook quick commands (notes to self)
- route:set-weight model-v2 0.6 -> fallback to model-v1 (check quality gate)
- enable-temporary-throttle tag:user-noncritical 0.5
- scale-dedicated-pool us-west-2 +2 nodes (confirm capacity is available)
- post-status "Investigating elevated latency"

Unresolved / discussion items:
- Quality gate tolerance for fallback: what is the exact threshold where routing to a lower-quality variant is allowed? currently conservatively set at 1.5x latency but need product signoff.
- Billing customer transparency: do we proactively alert customers about potential cost increases when scaling Dedicated for them? legal wants a template.
- Automation: which steps can safely be automated (e.g., weight adjustment) vs human-only? need a risk review.

Rehearsal plan and schedule:
- Week 1 (dry-run): internal-only simulation with fake load and no customer messages. Run with IL + Runtime + Model Routing.
- Week 2 (dress rehearsal): include CS and Comms, publish status page to a private test domain, notify a small set of internal test accounts.
- Week 3 (postmortem): assemble notes, identify gaps, update runbook + automation backlog (owners + ticket numbers).

Postmortem prompts (to include after event)
- Timeline of detection -> mitigation -> resolution.
- What manual actions were taken and why.
- Any missed signals or false positives.
- Customer impact list and outreach log.
- Automation candidates and follow-up tickets.

Quick TODOs (who/when)
- Azra: draft automation-risk rubric for weight adjustments (due 2026-03-20).
- Ravi: create loadgen job and default parameters (due 2026-03-18).
- Maya: prepare Slack + status page templates and host them in Confluence (due 2026-03-18).
- Jonas: confirm Dedicated pool headroom for dry-run region (due 2026-03-16).

Notes to self (personal reminders)
- Keep all templates short — support asks will escalate if verbose.
- Make one-click status page publish button obvious in Confluence.
- Coordinate with legal on the customer cost message before Week 2.

Potential risks to call out in the run:
- Automation triggers a cascade that affects regional fallbacks in unexpected ways (test this in staging ONLY).
- Model quality regressions when routing to older variants — ensure canary set of requests routed to check quality before full switch.
- Support overload: CS paging thresholds may need adjusting to avoid alert fatigue.

Slack channels and contacts to ping during run (short list):
- #ops-oncall (primary)
- #runtime-ops
- #cs-incident-team
- @ravi, @maya, @jonas for immediate ops tasks

Rough expected outcomes from dry-run:
- Validate timing assumptions (e.g., acknowledge in 2 min, mitigation in 15).
- Identify any missing playbook steps.
- Produce a short one-page playbook that can be copy-pasted into an incident channel.

End-of-file note: this is intentionally terse and chatty — will iterate into a polished Confluence runbook after two rehearsals.
